title: Tenant-aware FastPath Router and Spillback Circuit for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Ravi Shah
description: Problem: Dedicated fleets occasionally experience short-lived overloads due to bursty tenant traffic and synchronization between autoscaler cycles. Current admission proxies apply coarse per-fleet rate limits which lead to inefficient tail latency and poor fairness for latency-sensitive tenants. Goal: implement a tenant-aware ingress router that fast-paths small, latency-sensitive requests while absorbing large bursts via a spillback circuit and tenant credit smoothing. The system should preserve per-tenant minimum throughput guarantees, allow controlled best-effort bursting, and provide transparent metrics for rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Router accepts per-tenant SLA config and enforces minimum guaranteed qps with <1% violation over 1h under synthetic load
FastPath routes requests below size/latency heuristics to low-latency queue with 95th percentile serving latency improvement of >=20% for targeted tenants
Spillback circuit triggers when fleet headroom < configurable threshold and returns deterministic 429 or queued handoff depending on policy
Telemetry surfaces per-tenant reserved credits, burst consumption, slowpath queue depth, and shed events in Console (route-level dashboards)
Canary rollout succeeds: 10% of requests to dedicated fleet use new router for 48h with no increase in SLO violations compared to baseline
implementation_notes: Design a two-tier ingress: FastPath (in-memory, low-latency) + SlowPath (backpressure queue with tokenized leases)
Maintain per-tenant credit buckets with a sliding-window reservation and burst buffer; credits replenish from both steady reservation and predictive autoscaler hints
Spillback circuit uses sustained headroom estimate from autoscaler and a short-term EWMA of incoming qps to decide immediate spill or queueing
Integrate with existing admission layer: reuse ratequeue admission hooks and expose hook points for Dedicated autoscaler to provide future capacity hints
Expose control flags for policy: drop-only, queue-and-retry, or spill-to-fallback-model; map to tenant tiers (gold/silver/bronze)
Instrument end-to-end: token consumption, fastpath hit-rate, slowpath wait times, shed reasons; emit structured traces for tail analysis
Benchmark on a dedicated small fleet (4x V100 equivalent) with mixed tenants: 70% background batch, 30% latency-sensitive per-tenant 100-200 rps spikes
comments: 2025-03-20 - Ravi Shah: Initial ticket created after postmortem for spike on 2025-03-18. Observed simultaneous autoscaler churn and tenant burst — need a smoother ingress shim.

2025-03-24 - Lena Kim: Proposed architecture sketch posted to docs: https://drive.redwood.ai/d/ingress-fastpath-sketch (internal). Calling out interaction with autoscaler and required API for capacity hints.
2025-03-27 - SRE Review (Ava Martinez): Concern about complexity of predictive hints; recommended conservative default (hints are advisory) and circuit must be fail-safe to drop-only if hints absent.
2025-03-30 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 implementing core router and per-tenant token buckets. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821

2025-04-01 - Load test results: small fleet replay shows fastpath improves p95 by ~18% for latency tenants, but slowpath queue grew under synthetic pathological burst. Need tunable queue depth and backoff jitter. Logged follow-up tasks for tuning.
2025-04-03 - Design Review (PM: Nora Chen): Confirmed UX for Console: expose per-tenant credits and shed counters, and add an alert when hard-429 rate exceeds threshold. Added to acceptance criteria.
2025-04-04 - Engineering note: added metric exports and feature flag gating. Preparing canary rollout config for next deploy window.
rollout_plan: Start behind a feature flag. Phase 1: unit and integration tests + internal canary (10% traffic) for 48h. Phase 2: metrics review and expand to 50% over 72h. Phase 3: full rollout with default conservative policy. Provide hot rollback by toggling flag and fallback to existing admission proxy. Communicate to account managers for high-impact tenants prior to full rollout.
